outer_multicall_in_progress.meaning: an outer multicall batch operation is in progress
outer_multicall_in_progress.checkpoint: before the outer multicall loop executes its inner calls

inner_call_is_nested_multicall.meaning: one inner call of the outer multicall is a delegatecall to multicall itself
inner_call_is_nested_multicall.checkpoint: before the nested inner multicall executes

subsequent_call_requires_fee.meaning: a subsequent call in the outer multicall requires a nonzero fee specified in its call parameters
subsequent_call_requires_fee.checkpoint: before the subsequent fee-requiring call executes

legitimate_batch_completes.meaning: the legitimate batch transaction that follows the nested multicall and requires a fee completes successfully rather than failing
legitimate_batch_completes.checkpoint: after the outer multicall finishes processing the subsequent fee-requiring call

assumptions: The nested multicall and the subsequent fee-requiring call occur within the same outer multicall transaction.
The fee-requiring call's required fee is nonzero as specified in its call parameters.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the attacker must be authorized or whether anyone can call multicall; the scenario is treated as reachable by a malicious user without further authorization facts.
Report does not specify the exact fee amount or the msg.value/msgValue comparison operands beyond msg.value == msgValue.

limitations: The impact is potential: the plan formalizes only the report-supported conditional scenario in which a crafted nested multicall precedes a fee-requiring legitimate batch call.
The failure of the legitimate batch is represented as the negation of successful completion; the exact revert mechanism is not separately modeled.
The report's flag-reset root cause is not encoded as a precondition; only the observable scenario facts are used.
